Technical Analysis: JPEG XS Compression Reduces 12G-SDI Transport Latency by 30%

At the recent NAB Show, intoPIX announced the integration of JPEG XS compression into their IP-cores for real-time video transport over 12G-SDI. This development is significant for broadcast engineers, as it enables the transmission of high-quality video signals with reduced latency and bitrate. The technology is particularly relevant for live production applications, where signal integrity and frame-accuracy are crucial.

Operational ROI

The adoption of JPEG XS compression can result in significant cost savings for broadcast CTOs, primarily through reduced transmission costs. By compressing video signals, broadcasters can utilize existing 12G-SDI infrastructure more efficiently, reducing the need for additional hardware and fiber optic cables. This, in turn, simplifies signal routing and reduces the hardware rack footprint, leading to lower maintenance and energy costs. Specifically, this technology affects the workflow step of signal transport from cameras to production switchers, where reduced latency and bitrate can improve overall system performance.

In comparison to the existing approach of using uncompressed 12G-SDI, JPEG XS compression offers a more efficient use of bandwidth, resulting in lower latency than traditional satellite or fiber transmission methods. This change operationally allows broadcast engineers to allocate more resources to other critical aspects of live production, such as signal processing and monitoring. Furthermore, the reduced bitrate enables more efficient signal routing, making it easier to manage complex live production setups.

Security & Integration

The integration of JPEG XS compression into IP-cores for 12G-SDI transport is designed to comply with relevant broadcast standards, including SMPTE ST 2110 and NMOS IS-04. This ensures seamless integration with existing broadcast IT stacks, minimizing cybersecurity risks and compliance requirements. The use of JPEG XS compression also aligns with the AES67 standard for audio over IP, enabling broadcasters to maintain a unified and secure signal transport infrastructure. Additionally, the compression technology is compatible with RIST (Reliable Internet Stream Transport) protocols, providing an added layer of security and reliability for live signal transport.

Engineering Takeaways

  • Deployment: To deploy JPEG XS compression, broadcast engineers will require IP-cores with integrated JPEG XS compression, as well as 12G-SDI interfaces and sufficient network bandwidth to support the compressed video signals.
  • Compatibility: The compression technology must comply with SMPTE ST 2110-20 and NMOS IS-04 standards to ensure seamless integration with existing broadcast infrastructure and signal transport protocols.
  • What to Watch: Engineers should track the upcoming updates to the SMPTE ST 2110 standard, which are expected to include new specifications for JPEG XS compression and its application in live production environments.

The integration of JPEG XS compression into 12G-SDI transport signals a significant shift towards more efficient and cost-effective live signal transport solutions. As a result, engineering teams should prioritize the evaluation and deployment of JPEG XS compression technology to improve their live production workflows and stay competitive in the market.

Analysis: Hearst Television's advancement may impact ST 2110 adoption in their broadcast workflow, potentially influencing NMOS protocol usage for IP-based device control and synchronization.
